title: Fixed #21772 -- Restored template context layers on context manager exit.
body:
#### Trac ticket number

ticket-21772

#### Branch description

An included template whose custom tag calls `context.update()` without popping the added layer can leak the include's extra context into its parent. For example, rendering `{{ foo }}|{% include included with foo="bar" %}|{{ foo }}` with `foo="foo"` currently ends in `|bar` when the included template pushes another layer.

Make `ContextDict.__exit__()` pop through its own layer instead of popping only the topmost layer. Compare layers by identity so equal-valued dictionaries do not stop cleanup prematurely. This also restores the expected stack when nested context managers exit after an exception.

Add four regression tests covering `push()` and `update()`, multiple extra layers, equal-valued layers, nested exception cleanup, and an actual included template. Update the context API documentation and the 6.2 compatibility notes.

#### Validation

- Before the fix: all four new tests failed (five failures including the two push/update subtests); the include regression rendered `foo|barinner|bar` instead of `foo|barinner|foo`.
- Complete template test package: 1,581 tests passed the runner, with 7 skipped on the final run after installing optional dependencies.
- Black 26.5.1, isort 8.0.1, flake8 7.3.0, sphinx-lint, blacken-docs, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Complete HTML documentation build passed with `sphinx-build -b html -W --keep-going -q`.
- Full SQLite suite: 19,995 tests ran, with 1,527 skipped and 7 expected failures. The run reported 10 failures and 1 error.
- Two failures were development-version mismatches caused by creating the commit while the suite was running; both admin-script tests passed on rerun after the commit.
- The remaining 8 subtest failures and 1 error reproduced identically in an untouched archive of upstream commit `63d898b`: malformed-address handling in `mail.test_backends.SMTPBackendTests.test_avoids_sending_to_invalid_addresses`, two `utils_tests.test_html.TestUtilsHtml.test_strip_tags` cases, and bound/unbound warning-line assertions in `deprecation.test_warn_about_implementation` (`test_method`, `test_classmethod`, `test_decorated_method`). title: Fixed #37428 -- Added caching of HTTP QUERY responses.
body:
#### Trac ticket number

ticket-37428

#### Branch description

Follow-up to #37232 (HTTP `QUERY` support): `FetchFromCacheMiddleware`/`UpdateCacheMiddleware` and `cache_page()` now cache `QUERY` responses. This answers the three open questions on the ticket:

- **Cache key:** for `QUERY` requests the key also hashes the `Content-Type` and the raw request body, without parsing it, as required by RFC 10008 Section 2.7. `QUERY` entries use their own method component, so they never mix with cached `GET`/`HEAD` responses for the same URL.
- **Re-reading:** `FetchFromCacheMiddleware.process_request()` reads `request.body` before the view runs, so a view calling `request.read()` reads from the in-memory copy, and `learn_cache_key()` on a cold cache doesn't hit `RawPostDataException`. If an earlier middleware already consumed the stream, the request isn't cached.
- **Size limit:** a body over `DATA_UPLOAD_MAX_MEMORY_SIZE` means "don't cache". The middleware catches `RequestDataTooBig` and lets the view run as normal, so no new exceptions escape the middleware.

title: Fixed #37443 - Added a tasks email backend.
body:
#### Trac ticket number

ticket-37443

#### Branch description

Sending email during a request lengthens the response, which can expose information such as whether an account exists through timing (see the PasswordResetView warning). This adds `django.core.mail.backends.tasks.EmailBackend`, which lets projects move delivery to the background through `MAILERS`, without changing code that calls `send_mail()` or `EmailMessage.send()`. The backend enqueues a task that sends the messages using another configured mailer.

Messages are serialized to JSON since task arguments must be JSON-serializable. `send_messages()` returns the number of messages queued rather than sent, so delivery failures are reported by the task rather than to the caller (addressing the API concern raised on the ticket). If the task backend runs tasks immediately, failures are still raised to the caller.

Thanks David Smith for the report and Jake Howard for the discussion.

title: Fixed #37450 -- Fixed parsing of comment and verbatim tags without spaces.
body:
#### Trac ticket number

ticket-37450

#### Branch description
Since 1a9fba7a6c2a0acead19bbb45c25ceb0fdcca7c8, `_comment_end_re` and `_verbatim_end_re` require whitespace after `{%`, so `{%endcomment%}` and `{%endverbatim%}` never close a raw block, and `_raw_start_re` requires it before `comment`/`verbatim`, so with `debug=False` a `{%verbatim%}` block is not lexed as raw text. Templates such as `{% comment %}…{%endcomment%}` and `{%verbatim%}…{%endverbatim%}` then fail to parse or crash, `{%comment%}…{%endcomment%}` fails with `debug=True`, and `makemessages` drops strings that follow a `{% comment %}…{%endcomment%}` block. This allows zero whitespace in the three patterns, as the pattern for a named `endverbatim` already does.

title: Refs #36259 -- Adjusted generated-field errors and added warnings.
body:
#### Trac ticket number

ticket-36259

#### Branch description

This draft covers all four cases in the ticket. It is a proposal to discuss, not an agreed plan.

**Case 2 (generated fields), changed now:** reading an unloaded `GeneratedField` on a new instance raises `AttributeError` instead of `DoesNotExist` when no row matches. Lookups that find a row, `FETCH_RAISE`, and errors for saved instances don't change. This covers `FETCH_ONE` and `FETCH_PEERS` for a single instance.

**Cases 1, 3 and 4, warnings for now:** a new instance with a primary key set (`_state.adding` is `True`) now warns with `RemovedInDjango2029Warning` when it is:

* passed to a related `filter()` or `exclude()` (including `__in`),
* passed to `QuerySet.contains()` or `acontains()`, or
* the cached related object of a `ForeignKey` or `OneToOneField` in `save()`, `bulk_create()`, or `bulk_update()` (only for the fields being updated).

The check looks at `_state.adding`, not at whether a row exists, and adds no query. Results stay the same, unless warnings are turned into errors; then these calls stop at the warning. In these filter, `contains()`, and save calls, an instance without a primary key, or with a cleared one, still raises `ValueError`. Reverse related managers (reads), prefetching, inline formsets, and deletion now use the target field values, so they don't warn. The docs show what to use instead: target field values, raw foreign key values, or instances loaded from the database.

**Questions for maintainers:**

* Is `_state.adding` the right check? It also warns for valid code, such as a `pre_save` handler or a custom `clean()` that filters by a new instance with a default UUID primary key, a filter with a deserialized instance, a primary key that points to an existing row, and saving the related row later in the same transaction. (The `pre_save`, `clean()`, and deserialized examples come from small local scripts, not from new tests.)
* Should the generated-field change and the warnings be decided together, or split? Case 2 can still read a value from an existing row, while queries warn about a new instance that points to the same row.
* Is raising `ValueError` in Django 2029 OK? The docs mark this date as a proposal.

Known limits: for `acontains()` and `asave()`, the warning points to `asgiref/sync.py` (asgiref 3.13), not the caller. The `GenericForeignKey` save check doesn't change.

**Testing** on main at 0e128d5. Some of the new tests are guards that already pass on main.

| Database | New tests, main (60 / 75 generated-field) | New tests, this branch | Full test suite, this branch |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| SQLite | 32 warning failures / 9 errors | all pass | 20,017 pass |
| PostgreSQL 17 | 32 warning failures / 5 errors (31 skipped) | all pass (31 skipped) | 20,017 pass |
| MySQL 8.4 | 31 warning failures (2 skipped) / 9 errors | all pass (2 skipped) | 20,019 run, 1 error |
| Oracle 23 | 32 warning failures / 9 errors | all pass | not run |

The errors on main are the old `DoesNotExist`. The skips are database features: PostgreSQL 17 has no virtual generated columns, and MySQL can't defer constraint checks. The one MySQL error, `constraints.tests.UniqueConstraintTests.test_validate_case_when` (mixed collations), also fails on main with the same local settings, so it is not from this branch. `make check` and the HTML docs build pass.

title: Fixed #37395 -- Emitted 'none' for CSP directives left empty by an unused nonce.
body:

ticket-37395

#### Branch description

When a CSP directive's only source is `CSP.NONCE` and the nonce is never used while rendering a response, removing the nonce sentinel left the directive empty and it was silently omitted from the header, so the browser fell back to less restrictive directives (e.g. `script-src: [CSP.NONCE]` disappeared and scripts fell back to `default-src`).

title: Fixed silent drop of CSP directive whose only value is the nonce sentinel. (#37441)
body:
#### Trac ticket number

ticket-37441

#### Branch description

Fixed silent drop of CSP directive whose only value is the nonce sentinel.

`build_policy()` removes `CSP.NONCE` placeholders when no nonce is generated for the request (the nonce is only created when something actually accesses it, e.g. the `csp_nonce` template context key). The current code does:

```python
values = [v for v in values if v != CSP.NONCE]
```

...but when the sentinel was the **only** value of a directive, that leaves an empty list, and the `if not values: continue` guard then skips the directive entirely.

With

```python
SECURE_CSP = {
    "default-src": ["'self'"],
    "script-src": [CSP.NONCE],
}
```

a request/response that never evaluates the nonce (a pure API view, a streamed response, any nonces-never-accessed path) ships:

```
Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self';
```

`script-src` silently disappears and the browser restricts scripts with whatever `default-src` (or nothing — a sentinel-only `SECURE_CSP` produces **no CSP header at all**) would have allowed. The developer configuring a nonce-only `script-src` intends a fail-closed position: only nonce-bearing scripts may run. The current behavior fails **open**, weakening the configured policy.

## Fixed

When the sentinel is removed and it was the sole value, substitute `CSP.NONE` so the directive remains present and restrictive:

| input | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `{"script-src": CSP.NONCE}`, no nonce | *(directive dropped)* | `script-src 'none'` |
| `{"default-src": "'self'", "script-src": [CSP.NONCE]}`, no nonce | `default-src 'self'` | `default-src 'self'; script-src 'none'` |
| `{"script-src": [CSP.NONCE]}`, nonce present | `script-src 'nonce-…'` | unchanged |

`'none'` (rather than an empty directive value) is deliberate: it is unambiguous across browsers, while an empty source list has heterogeneous historical handling.

title: Fixed #36833 -- Made split_header_value() respect quoted strings.
body:
#### Trac ticket number

ticket-36833

#### Branch description
`split_header_value()` split on every comma, including commas inside quoted strings. For example, `patch_cache_control(response, no_cache=True)` turned an existing `no-cache="Set-Cookie, Link"` (the RFC 9111 qualified form) into `no-cache, link"`, and `split_directive_names('example="alpha, public, omega"')` reported a `public` directive that isn't there. `HttpRequest.accepted_types` had the same problem with quoted media type parameters, e.g. `Accept: text/plain; param="a,b", application/json`.

Changes:
- `split_header_value()` now ignores separators inside quoted strings and honors backslash escapes within them (RFC 9110, Section 5.6.4). Values without a double quote, which includes every valid `Vary` value and typical `Cache-Control` values, keep the previous `str.split()` path, so the common case costs the same as before (locally about 0.7 µs for a typical `Vary` value, on both main and this branch). The quoted path is a single linear pass (about 3.5 ms for 50,000 commas inside quotes).
- `HttpRequest.accepted_types` now uses `split_header_value()`.
- `parse_etags()` goes back to splitting on every comma, as it did before `split_header_value()` was added. In an entity-tag, a backslash is an ordinary character, not an escape (RFC 9110, Section 8.8.3), so the quoted-string-aware split would merge `"a\", "b"` into one invalid entry and drop both ETags. Its behavior is unchanged, and a test now covers this case.

Alternatives considered:
- `email.message.Message`, which `parse_header_parameters()` uses since #35440, only splits `;`-separated parameters. It can't split a top-level comma list: `get_params()` on `text/plain; param="a,b", application/json` returns the param value as `'"a,b", application/json'`.
- `urllib.request.parse_http_list()` handles quoted commas, but it isn't documented, only supports `,`, and drops backslash escapes. That would change values that `patch_cache_control()` writes back: `private="a\"b"` becomes `private="a"b"`.

No release note, as this bug fix targets the main branch only.

title: Fixed #36588 -- Hardened TarArchive.extract with minimal data filter
body:
#### Trac ticket number

ticket-36588

#### Branch description

Complementary hardening for #36588, with no overlap with the size/count limits effort (this patch adds no size or count accounting).

`TarArchive.extract()` currently passes every non-directory member to `extractfile()` + `copyfileobj()`. Two failure modes, both reproduced with PoCs on 5.2.18 (the function is identical on main):

1. Device/fifo members: `extractfile()` returns `None`, so `copyfileobj(None)` raises `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'read'`, leaves a 0-byte file behind, and aborts the whole extraction (`ok.txt` never extracted).
2. Corrupt symlink as first member: `extracted` is never assigned, so the `finally: if extracted:` block raises `UnboundLocalError`, masking the original error. (When a later member is corrupt, the stale previous value gets wrongly `close()`d — order-dependent.)

In addition, invalid-member notices go to `print()` instead of `warnings`.

This patch (11 insertions, 2 deletions, one file):

- Skips non-regular, non-directory members (`if not member.isreg() and not member.isdir(): continue`) — a minimal `tarfile` `filter='data'` equivalent. Symlinks/hardlinks are not materialized, devices/fifos are skipped, so neither the `AttributeError` path nor temp-file residue can occur.
- Initializes `extracted = None`, continues when `extractfile()` returns `None`, and checks `is not None` in `finally` — no more `UnboundLocalError`, no stale close.
- Routes the invalid-member notice through `warnings.warn()`.

Verified: device/fifo tar now extracts `ok.txt` with no residue and no exception; corrupt-first symlink tar no longer raises `UnboundLocalError`; normal tars extract unchanged. Existing `tests/utils_tests/test_archive.py` behavior unchanged (no size/count behavior changed).

Suggested tests: fifo skipped, symlink skipped, corrupt-first no `UnboundLocalError`, normal-tar regression.

title: Fixed #37435 -- Sped up post-commit callback dispatch.
body:
#### Trac ticket number

ticket-37435

#### Branch description

Post-commit callbacks are currently removed with pop(0), which shifts the remaining list each time. That makes queue-management overhead O(N²).

This keeps the existing list-detachment step, walks the list once, and clears each slot before calling its callback. Queue-management overhead becomes O(N), without building a second queue. The callbacks' own execution time is separate.

Clearing slots matters here: a plain loop would keep completed callbacks alive in the list. This version drops each queue reference before execution, including when a later callback raises and its traceback is kept. The existing robust/nonrobust exception-handling block is unchanged.

The list still keeps its allocated slots until the dispatcher frame is released. A saved traceback can still retain the failing callback and callbacks that have not run. Also, an external alias to this private detached list would now see cleared slots rather than a shrinking list; this does not preserve private-list introspection or direct mutation during dispatch.

Checks run locally on Python 3.14.5 with SQLite:

- The same 195 focused tests ran on the original and changed implementations, with no failures and the same 10 skips. These cover transaction_hooks, transactions and backends.base.
- Five new regression tests cover failure ordering and committed data, BaseException, callback release before the next callback, retained failure tracebacks, and retained robust-error logs.
- 468 before/after comparisons matched callback order, exception/log outcomes, queue state and transaction state.
- Black, isort, flake8 and git diff --check passed on the changed files.

The benchmark table below includes all 48 measured rows, including slower cases. It measures complete SQLite transactions, callback registration and dictionary-update callbacks, not model writes or network/broker calls. Larger queues showed gains, but tiny cases were not consistently faster. The earlier plain-loop prototype's roughly 12% extra peak-memory result is not a result for this slot-clearing version.

title: Fixed #37431 -- Preserved frozendict values in migration serialization.
body:
#### Trac ticket number

ticket-37431

#### Branch description

Preserved keys and values when serializing Python 3.15 built-in `frozendict` instances into migrations.

Previously, `MigrationWriter` treated `frozendict` as a generic iterable, silently discarding its values:

    MigrationWriter.serialize(frozendict(answer=42))
    # Before: ("('answer',)", set())
    # After:  ("frozendict({'answer': 42})", set())

This affects field defaults. On SQLite, executing a generated `AddField` migration for `JSONField(default=frozendict(answer=42))` populated existing rows with `["answer"]` instead of `{"answer": 42}`.

The change adds a dedicated serializer and regression tests covering empty and nested mappings, values requiring imports, field defaults, and execution of a generated migration against an existing row. The regression tests failed before applying the fix.

Documentation and release notes explain that migrations containing `frozendict` require Python 3.15+.

title: Fixed #37427 -- Kept generic relation queryset routing lazy.
body:
Generic relation managers stored the read router's database choice as a queryset alias. This made an implicit route trigger the cross-database subquery guard when the outer query selected another connection.

Kept routing lazy by passing the related instance as a router hint, while preserving explicit database selections. Added regression coverage and documented database selection for IN subqueries.

#### Trac ticket number

[ticket-37427](https://code.djangoproject.com/ticket/37427)

#### Branch description

Generic relation managers eagerly select a database through the read router and bind the queryset to it using `.using(db)`, even when no database was explicitly selected by the caller.

When this queryset is used in an `__in` subquery, the implicit database choice can conflict with the outer query’s connection and raise:

> Subqueries aren't allowed across different databases.

This can happen in primary/replica configurations, for example:

```python
Review.objects.filter(pk__in=book.reviews.all())
```

Updated generic relation managers to pass the related instance as a routing hint and only bind the database when an alias was explicitly selected, matching ordinary related managers.

Implicit subqueries now use the outer query’s connection. Standalone reads retain instance-aware routing, and explicitly conflicting `.using()` or `.db_manager()` selections continue to raise the existing error.

Added regression coverage for subquery execution, standalone routing, and explicit database selections, along with documentation explaining database selection for `__in` subqueries.

title: Fixed #24523 -- Allowed retrying Apps.populate() after a failure.
body:
#### Trac ticket number

ticket-24523

#### Branch description
If an `AppConfig.ready()` method raised an exception, e.g. because the database was briefly unavailable, the registry stayed in its "loading" state. Every later call to `populate()` then raised `RuntimeError: populate() isn't reentrant`, hiding the original error. This affects servers like mod_wsgi that import the application again in the same process after a failure.

Following Carl's suggestion in [comment:16](https://code.djangoproject.com/ticket/24523#comment:16), calling `populate()` again after a failure in phase 3 now resumes with the `ready()` method that failed:
- `ready()` methods that already succeeded aren't called again.
- Phases 1 and 2 aren't repeated, so no module is imported again and model classes aren't redefined.

Failures in phases 1 and 2 (importing app or models modules) keep the current behavior, since importing a partially executed models module again would redefine model classes that other models may already reference.

title: Fixed #35965 -- Updated GenericForeignKey fk_field when saving after related object is saved.
body:
#### Trac ticket number

#### Branch description

When an unsaved model instance is assigned to a `GenericForeignKey`, `fk_field` (`object_id`) is initially set to `None`. This change updates `Model._prepare_related_fields_for_save()` to re-assign the cached related object on the `GenericForeignKey` when `fk_field` is empty, matching the behavior of `ForeignKey`.

title: Fixed #37402 -- Prevented AttributeError in QuerySet.first() and last() when grouping by annotations.
body:
#### Trac ticket number

#### Branch description

When calling `.first()` or `.last()` on an unordered queryset performing aggregation and grouping by an annotation (such as using `Lower()` in `annotate()`), `_check_ordering_first_last_queryset_aggregation()` crashed with:

title: Fixed #37416 -- Fixed atomic migration recording when deferred SQL is present
body:
### Summary

Fixes #37416.

### Problem & Background

Django previously recorded applied migrations inside the schema editor context to keep schema changes and their corresponding entries in `django_migrations` within the same transaction.

However, #32374 moved migration recording outside the schema editor context when deferred SQL was present. This was necessary to ensure that a migration would not be recorded as applied if executing its deferred SQL failed.

The change introduced an atomicity issue. Deferred SQL is executed when the schema editor context exits, so the database transaction may commit before Django records the migration. If the process crashes or recording fails during this interval, the schema changes remain in the database even though Django has no record that the migration was applied.

This can cause Django to attempt the migration again, potentially failing because the schema objects already exist. Recording migrations outside the transaction also adds unnecessary overhead when a squashed migration records many replaced migrations individually.

### Solution

- Added `execute_deferred_sql()` to `BaseDatabaseSchemaEditor` to execute pending deferred SQL statements and clear the list.
- Updated `BaseDatabaseSchemaEditor.__exit__()` to use the new method, preserving the existing deferred SQL execution behavior.
- Updated `MigrationExecutor.apply_migration()` to execute deferred SQL and record the migration before exiting the schema editor context.
- Applied the same approach to `MigrationExecutor.unapply_migration()` to keep migration reversal and its recording consistent.
- Ensured that deferred SQL is executed before migration recording, so a deferred SQL failure prevents the migration from being recorded prematurely.
- Added regression tests for atomic migration recording during application and reversal, along with a unit test for deferred SQL execution.

### Testing

- Added `test_migrations_applied_and_recorded_atomically_deferred_sql` in `tests/migrations/test_executor.py`.
- Added `test_migrations_unapplied_and_recorded_atomically` in `tests/migrations/test_executor.py`.
- Added `test_execute_deferred_sql` in `tests/schema/tests.py`.
- [Add the actual results of the relevant migration, schema, and backend test suites.]

Keep migration changes and migration records atomic when deferred SQL is present.

title: Fixed #35482 -- Added dir="ltr" to EmailInput and URLInput widgets.

#### Branch description
In Right-to-Left (RTL) locales (such as Arabic, Hebrew, and Persian), form elements inherit `dir="rtl"`. However, email addresses and URLs are inherently Left-to-Right (LTR) data structures.

A [recent Windows run on `main`](https://github.com/django/django/actions/runs/37956026298/job/113906631270) installs gettext v1.0.0.20260310 to `C:\Program Files\gettext-iconv\` and then reports `skipped 'msgfmt is mandatory for compilation tests'` and `skipped 'xgettext is mandatory for extraction tests'`.

#22077 appended the bin directory with `echo "..." >> $GITHUB_PATH`. The Windows job doesn't set a shell, so its steps run under `pwsh`, where `$GITHUB_PATH` is an undefined PowerShell variable rather than the environment variable. The redirect target is `$null`, so the output is discarded and the step still succeeds. This PR writes to `$env:GITHUB_PATH` with `Out-File -Append`, as in GitHub's PowerShell examples.

With the tools on `PATH`, `PoFileTests.test_no_write_access` fails on Windows because `chmod()` can't make a directory read-only there, so it's skipped on Windows like the other chmod-based tests (e.g. `staticfiles_tests.test_storage.TestStaticFilePermissions`).

Checked locally on Windows 11 with Python 3.14 and the same gettext 1.0 build that Chocolatey installs:

- `runtests.py i18n` without gettext on `PATH` (current CI): 244 tests, `OK (skipped=91)`.
- `runtests.py i18n` with gettext on `PATH`: 244 tests, `OK (skipped=1)`, the remaining skip being `test_no_write_access`. Without the skip, it fails with `AssertionError: CommandError not raised`.
- Running the step's script under PowerShell 7.6 writes `C:\Program Files\gettext-iconv\bin` to the `GITHUB_PATH` file, whereas the `echo ... >> $GITHUB_PATH` form writes nothing and exits with 0.

title: Fixed #25245 -- Kept negated Q lookup correlation independent of branch order.
body:
#### Trac ticket number

ticket-25245

#### Branch description

A filter combining positive and negated reverse-FK lookups can return an extra row when OR or AND branches are reordered. The negative subquery can correlate to a child join introduced by an earlier sibling, so its meaning depends on how the Q tree is built.

Keep the inherited alias set stable for negative subquery correlation throughout Q recursion. Continue sharing aliases for ordinary joins, and preserve correlation for aliases referenced by right-hand expressions. The regressions cover both branch orders, multiple related rows, absent relations and same-row F comparisons.

- The new branch-order regression fails on untouched query implementation at `ce285ce0e755abbdd991e707b7aaf4d3c636e944` for positive-first OR and AND; the final patch passes both branch orders and the same-row F-expression guard.

- The first full run under CPython 3.12.3 reported eight failures and one error in five methods outside the changed query tests. All nine entries reproduced when those five methods were rerun on the untouched base with the same runtime. Under CPython 3.13.16, the five-method recheck and the full candidate SQLite suite both pass.

title: Fixed #37400 - Added metadata API to Tasks
body:
#### Trac ticket number

ticket-37400

#### Branch description

Added metadata support to tasks: a JSON-compatible dict stored alongside a task, separate from its arguments.

- Set via `Task.using(metadata={...})`.
- Read and modified within a task via `TaskContext.metadata`. Changes are saved when the task finishes (successfully or not), or explicitly with `TaskContext.save_metadata()` / `asave_metadata()`.
- Backends opt in with the `supports_metadata` feature flag and by implementing `save_metadata()` and/or `asave_metadata()`. `DummyBackend` and `ImmediateBackend` support it.
- Keys starting with `_` are reserved. They're stored in `TaskResult.raw_metadata`, hidden from `TaskResult.metadata` and `TaskContext.metadata`, and preserved when users save metadata.

Open questions for reviewers:
- Naming of the new public attributes `TaskResult.raw_metadata` and `TaskContext.metadata_modified`.
- Whether `save_metadata()` should receive only user keys and let the backend merge in its stored reserved keys. Currently reserved keys come from the in-memory result, which could overwrite newer values written by a backend while the task runs.

title: Fixed #29504 -- Documented limitations of integer-like keys in JSONField.
body:
#### Trac ticket number

ticket-29504

#### Branch description

This PR updates `docs/topics/db/queries.txt` to document the limitations of querying `JSONField` dictionaries that have integer-like keys (e.g. `{"0": "value"}`). It clarifies that integer keys are interpreted as array index transforms, meaning queries like `data__0="value"` do not match dictionary keys, and notes that chained lookups (`data__0__nested`) only work on PostgreSQL and are not portable across databases.
